messages:
Marcus Li: Hey everyone, Marcus here — first day! Quick hit: I enrolled an Okta passkey on my phone and accepted the 1Password invite, but two blockers: I can't ssh to `git@bastion.redwood` (Permission denied), and I don't see the shared /Engineering Drive folder from the onboarding doc. Also `op` CLI initially said \"membership not found\". Who do I ping for each?
sarah-it: welcome Marcus! Ping the #new-hires thread is perfect. For the Drive folder, check your Google groups membership first. For SSH: do you have an SSH public key uploaded to Okta (Profile -> Security -> SSH keys)? Okta passkeys != SSH keys.
Marcus Li: I just tried `ssh -T git@bastion.redwood` and get:
```
OpenSSH_9.2p1, OpenSSL 3.1.0
debug1: Offering public key: /home/marcus/.ssh/id_ed25519
debug1: Server accepts key: ssh-ed25519 SHA256:xxxx
debug1: Authentications that can continue: publickey
Permission denied (publickey).
```
So the key was offered but still denied.
lena-sre: that usually means the key isn't in the Okta SSH keys list or didn't sync to our ssh-provisioner. Marcus, can you confirm the contents of `~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub` (single line) and that you uploaded it to Okta -> Profile -> Security -> SSH keys? If you uploaded, allow ~90s for sync, then run `ssh -vvv git@bastion.redwood` and paste the last 10 lines.
Marcus Li: I uploaded the pubkey moments ago. Also, 1Password bot said my seat was assigned earlier: it-bot: 1Password seat granted to Marcus Li (marcus@redwood.com). But `op signin` still failed until I did `eval $(op signin --account redwood)` like the doc said. After that `op` works.
it-bot: 1Password seat assigned to Marcus Li (marcus@redwood.com) — invite accepted.
sarah-it: for Drive, I checked: your account provisioned but you are not in the `eng-general` Google group that grants the /Engineering shared drive. Adding you now.
sarah-it: done. You should see the folder within 60-120s. If not, try clearing cache or incognito.
Marcus Li: Drive appeared, can open the onboarding checklist, thanks. Back to SSH: I waited ~2 minutes but `ssh -vvv` still shows `Permission denied`. Pasting the end of the verbose log here:
```
debug1: Offering public key: /home/marcus/.ssh/id_ed25519
debug1: Server accepts key: ssh-ed25519 SHA256:xxxx
debug1: Authenticating with public key
debug1: key_load_private_type: invalid format
debug1: No more authentication methods available.
Permission denied (publickey).
```
lena-sre: ah, `key_load_private_type: invalid format` means your private key file might be encrypted with an unsupported format (or corrupted). Can you run `ssh-keygen -y -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` to print the public key (if private key is valid)? If that errors, regenerate with `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C \"marcus@redwood.com\"` and re-upload the new pubkey to Okta.
Marcus Li: `ssh-keygen -y -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` failed with `invalid private key file`. I must have mangled it when copying between machines. Regenerating now and will re-upload.
amanda-devex: FYI — if you regenerate, remember to update any machines that need the old key. We recommend using passphrases + ssh-agent. I can DM you our laptop bootstrap script (dotfiles + ssh-agent config).
Marcus Li: regenerated and uploaded the new `id_ed25519.pub` (single-line), waiting for sync...
lena-sre: got the new key in the provisioner, try again now.
Marcus Li: sweet — SSH works! `git clone` succeeded. Thanks all :rocket:
sarah-it: glad it's sorted. Two small notes for the thread: 1) Okta passkeys are for web SSO only; they do not replace machine SSH keys. 2) 1Password seats sometimes need the `eval $(op signin ...)` step for the CLI to pick up creds.
Marcus Li: noted, thanks. Appreciate the quick help. Amanda, would love that bootstrap script.
amanda-devex: sending DM with script and a short checklist (install homebrew, X, add SSH key to Okta). Welcome again!
